questions.prompt: What is the intent of the Prototype pattern?

options.text: Create new objects by copying an existing prototypical instance
Ensure only one instance of a class exists
Build a complex object step by step
Provide a simplified interface to a subsystem

questions.explanation: Prototype creates objects by cloning. One instance = Singleton; step-by-step = Builder; simplified interface = Facade.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between a shallow copy and a deep copy?

options.text: A shallow copy shares nested objects; a deep copy duplicates every level so nothing is shared
A shallow copy is always slower than a deep copy
A deep copy shares nested objects; a shallow copy duplicates everything
They are the same thing

questions.explanation: Shallow duplicates only the top level (nested objects are shared); deep duplicates all levels.

questions.prompt: Why is a clone() that does `Object.assign(new Thing(), this)` often a bug?

options.text: It is a shallow copy, so the clone shares the original's nested objects and arrays
It always throws an exception
It creates two singletons
It permanently freezes the original

questions.explanation: Top-level assignment leaves nested references shared, so mutating one 'copy' changes the other.

questions.prompt: Which statements about structuredClone() are TRUE? Select all that apply.

options.text: It performs a deep copy of plain data
It preserves a class instance's methods and prototype
It cannot clone functions
It returns a plain object when given a class instance

questions.explanation: structuredClone deep-copies data but drops methods/prototype (returns a plain object) and can't clone functions.

questions.prompt: How does the Prototype pattern relate to JavaScript's prototypal inheritance?

options.text: They share a name but are different ideas: the pattern copies objects, prototypal inheritance shares behavior via a linked prototype
They are exactly the same mechanism
Prototypal inheritance is a way to guarantee a single instance
The pattern only works in languages without prototypes

questions.explanation: The Prototype pattern is about cloning; JS prototypal inheritance is a language feature for sharing methods. Same word, different concept.

When you must forbid copying entirely
When an object should have exactly one instance
When two incompatible interfaces must work together
